title: Machine learning selects CeCoBi and CeIrBi for thermoelectric calculations
summary: An ICGM-led study used learned SISSO descriptors and other machine-learning models to screen half-Heusler compositions, selecting CeCoBi and CeIrBi for first-principles follow-up. The October 9, 2026 arXiv v2 reports calculated intrinsic power factors of 5.26 and 8.39 mW m−1 K−2 at 673 K under a constant relaxation-time assumption. These calculations support electronic transport potential, not measured performance, complete stability or the predicted thermoelectric figure of merit: lattice thermal conductivity, phase/mechanical/dynamical stability and synthesis remain for later work. A February 1 preprint already described the screening workflow; the journal accepted the work on November 20.
ai_technology: SISSO symbolic regression; random forest; XGBoost; neural networks; Bayesian hyperparameter optimization
organization: Institute Charles Gerhardt Montpellier, University of Montpellier; CNRS; ENSCM

evidence.tested: Within-study DFT electronic-structure and transport calculations for two SISSO-selected compositions; power factors assume relaxation time10−14s. CeCoBi is calculated narrow-gap and CeIrBi semimetallic.
evidence.unknown: The authors explicitly defer full phase, mechanical and dynamical stability and lattice thermal conductivity calculations. No synthesized materials, measured power factors or complete DFT zT validation are established.
evidence.ai_role: SISSO predicts high zT for CeCoBi and CeIrBi from learned descriptor–property relations; these selections motivate their explicit DFT follow-up.
